name: Client support desk
summary: A light support desk: tickets with a priority, a first-response time and a due time, known issues that link many tickets to one cause, and a satisfaction score.
description: Answer customers and clients from one place: every ticket has a status, a priority, a type, an owner and the time by which you owe a first reply and a solution. Link tickets to a known issue so you can tell everyone when it is fixed, and keep the one-month clock of a data request visible. It is built for a few dozen tickets a week. It is not a phone system, a live chat, a customer portal or a business-hours calendar.

prompt.intro: Set up a client support desk in my Customermates workspace: tickets with a status, a priority, a first-reply time and a solution time, known issues linked to tickets, a satisfaction rating and dated follow-ups.
questions: How many tickets do you handle a week, and through which channels do they arrive?
How fast do you promise a first reply and a solution, by priority or support plan?
Who answers, and who is told when a ticket is late?
Do you get data requests or alerts from other systems that should become tickets?
